title: Onboarding latency-cost curves and regression holdouts
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and intermediate results from the onboarding experiments for new model variants (open-chat-13b-v2 and rw-opt-lite-7b). We're trying to map out the latency / cost / quality tradeoff surface as we sweep batching, prefix/KV cache behavior, and max_tokens limits. Goal is to produce simple heuristics and a small set of recommended defaults that the Console can surface for new model entries and Dedicated capacity SKUs.

High-level approach
---
1) Take representative prompt sets (long-form summarization, short Q&A, conversational turn continuation). Keep a held-out regression set (10% of prompts) to catch quality regressions after later quant/optim flags are applied.
2) Run controlled sweeps across: batch_size in {1,2,4,8,16}; max_tokens in {16,64,128,256,512}; cache_policy in {no-cache, prefix-only, kv-cache}.
3) Collect latency percentiles (p50, p95), throughput (tokens/s), and estimated token cost per 1k output tokens (using our internal unit pricing model). Also record exact quality metrics per prompt set (ROUGE-L for summarization, EM/F1 for short-QA, and a conversational coherence score, all measured against reference answers).
4) Fit a cost-latency-quality frontier and record the knee-points where latency increases greatly for small quality gains.

Experimental setup details
---
- Hardware: Dedicated single-GPU node (A100S 80GB equivalence) with the serving runtime v0.18.3. For Dedicated-representative runs we also did a 2x node test to validate autoscaling effects.
- Serving config: seq_len = 2048 default, kv_cache_enabled toggled per sweep. Use continuous batching (runtime default) and synthetic arrival pattern matching production 75th-percentile inter-arrival time.
- Tokens counted: output tokens only for cost calculation; prompts/priming tokens tracked for latency analysis but excluded from cost-per-output unit.
- Prompt sets: 4 files. Summarize-long (200 prompts, average prompt tokens 420), ShortQA (400 prompts, avg 30 tokens), Chat-Continuations (300 multi-turn snippets, avg 120 tokens).

Representative results (summary)
---
- Batch size effects: p50 latency improves smoothly up to batch=8 for all models. p95 latency improves through batch=4 but shows diminishing returns thereafter; batch=16 increased p95 tail for Chat-Continuations due to KV cache interference (see notes). Throughput (tokens/s) plateaued at batch=8 for rw-opt-lite-7b and batch=4 for open-chat-13b-v2.
- Max_tokens: Increasing max_tokens from 64->256 raised p95 by ~10-35% depending on prompt length distribution; cost per output token rises linearly but quality gains saturate after 128 for Summarize-long.
- Cache policy: prefix-only caching gave the best latency wins for Summarize-long (avg 18% p95 reduction) because prompts share long common prefixes in that set. KV-cache gave the largest throughput boost on multi-turn chat but required careful memory budgeting — it increased p95 tails under high concurrency when memory eviction kicked in.

Small textual table (aggregated; values are medians across prompts):

Model | Batch | Cache | max_toks | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | tokens/s | cost_per_1k_out
open-chat-13b-v2 | 1 | no-cache | 128 | 210 | 980 | 21.4 | $4.8
open-chat-13b-v2 | 4 | prefix | 128 | 120 | 520 | 73.2 | $3.1
rw-opt-lite-7b | 4 | kv-cache | 64 | 95 | 400 | 92.6 | $2.6
rw-opt-lite-7b | 8 | kv-cache | 128 | 110 | 610 | 145.9 | $3.5

Key observations and hypotheses
---
- Knee points differ by model family: opt-style smaller models gain more from batching (batch=8) while transformer-dense larger families (13B) saturate earlier. Hypothesis: larger models' per-token compute is dominated by attention kernel latency which doesn't vectorize as well for large batch sizes in our runtime.
- Max_tokens interacts non-linearly with p95 because the runtime's token generation loop has occasional heavy tails when attention window expansion or kv-cache management occurs.
- Prefix caching is high ROI only when prompt repetition exists. Generic prompt sets (user-generated app prompts) showed <5% improvement with prefix-only caching. So default recommendation should be conditional: enable prefix caches for onboarding profiles when prompt similarity > 25% based on trivial SHA1-prefix fingerprinting.

Regression holdout behavior
---
- We kept 10% of prompts as a locked regression bucket. After runs with quantization experiments (8-bit/fused kernels) we observed a small but measurable drop in ROUGE-L on Summarize-long (avg delta -1.8) for rw-opt-lite-7b 4-bit quant. This would have been missed if we only tracked aggregate token-level perplexity.
- Action: keep a minimum of two reference metrics per prompt set (one lexical like ROUGE/EM and one semantic classifier score) to ensure we catch mode collapse or hallucination regressions.

Operational recommendations (for Console defaults)
---
1) Suggested default profile for new model onboarding: batch=4, cache_policy=prefix-if-similarity>25%, max_tokens=128. Rationale: reasonable latency/throughput for both short and long prompt distributions without large P95 regressions.
2) When model is added to Dedicated SKU page, show an optional guided run: "Quick latency sweep" (batch 1,4,8; prefix/no-prefix; max_tokens 64/256) that completes in ~30 minutes and populates a short curve for the team.
3) For regression monitoring: require customers to provide or accept a default holdout prompt set (we provide templates). Alert if ROUGE/EM changes by >2.0 absolute points or semantic score delta >0.03.
4) Autoscale heuristic change: when KV-cache is enabled, prefer conservative concurrency limits (reduce allowed inflight requests by ~20%) to avoid memory-eviction-induced latency tails.

Notes / TODOs / open questions
---
- TODO: run the same sweep on multi-node Dedicated config to validate autoscaling heuristics (JIRA-APPLIED-321).
- TODO: formalize the prompt-similarity metric to decide prefix-caching eligibility and add telemetry to measure actual hit rates in production.
- Open: confirm cost modeling alignment with billing - our cost_per_1k_out is internal-estimated; need finance signoff before surfacing in Console. (CON-8772)
- Idea: "adaptive max_tokens" that drops output limit progressively if p95 crosses threshold with the same request — risk: changes output quality. Worth a short A/B pilot.

Appendix: short checklist for onboards
---
- [ ] Generate three representative prompt sets (short, long, conversational)
- [ ] Lock 10% regression holdout
- [ ] Run sweep (batch, cache, max_tokens) and save raw traces
- [ ] Produce knee-plot and recommended profile
- [ ] Create a Console quick-sweep link and PR for model entry

Raw traces and detailed numeric CSVs are attached in PR #412 (benchmarks) for anyone who wants to re-run. If you're taking this on: reach out to Evan for the runner scripts and to Luis for the cost mapping table.

Notes-to-self: draft will be ported to Confluence once stable defaults are agreed and finance confirms cost figures.
